edition: Issue #002 — bunker beats Warriors, AI nearly starts a war, one villa nobody needed
tagline: Your 3-minute break. Zero fluff, maximum banter.

stories.headline: Warriors' 2026 season ends 12-10 to Newcastle at a sold-out Eden Park
stories.summary: A record Eden Park crowd watched the Warriors bow out in straight sets after a Bunker call went against them in the final minute.

body.text: The Warriors' 2026 NRL campaign is over. Newcastle beat them 12-10 in a Finals Week Two thriller at Eden Park on Sunday night, in front of a record crowd of 48,511 — the ground was shifted there specifically to fit more fans in. Leka Halasima scored twice on essentially one leg, Newcastle held on, and a contested no-penalty call in the last minute will be replayed in Auckland living rooms for weeks.

Cool detail: the Bunker reviewed a Warriors captain's challenge, upheld it, reviewed a Newcastle one, upheld that too, and somehow the only call that didn't get reviewed was the one everyone's still yelling about at the servo. Truly the video ref system giveth, and the video ref system taketh away, mostly from Auckland.

Final score Warriors 10, Knights 12, at Eden Park on Sunday 20 September — sources: NRL.com live coverage and Brisbane Times match report, both citing the crowd of 48,511 and the disputed non-penalty on Leka Halasima in the final minute.

stories.headline: A false AI intelligence report nearly triggered a US–China military incident
stories.summary: US forces came close to boarding a Chinese ship over a nuclear-weapons claim that turned out to be an AI-generated error.

body.text: A false intelligence report, generated by AI, brought US forces close to boarding a Chinese vessel in the Middle East after the system flagged it as carrying nuclear weapons components — a claim that wasn't true. Military aircraft were reportedly on standby before it was walked back.

So the plan was: speed up military decision-making with AI, and the AI's first big swing was almost starting a war over cargo that wasn't there. Ten out of ten for confidence, zero out of ten for cargo manifests. This is why you don't let the intern near the launch codes, even a very fast intern.

Reported by the Daily Telegraph UK, via NZ Herald (21 Sep 2026): a Department of War official confirmed the military monitors and analyses hundreds of potential threats daily and said it remains "committed to rigorous verification of all intelligence inputs" amid a push to expand AI use in defence decision-making, a push officials themselves flagged risks around.

stories.headline: Herne Bay villa linked to property boss Chris Meehan sells for $14m, off-market
stories.summary: A five-bedroom villa with a $6.8m rating value quietly changed hands for double that, no open listing required.

body.text: A Herne Bay villa owned by a company linked to property developer Chris Meehan has sold for $14 million in an off-market deal — more than double its $6.8m rating valuation. It's not even the street's record; a villa two doors down got $15m last year, and the suburb's overall high is $38m for a waterfront pad.

Nothing says 'the market is tough for everyone' quite like a house getting $14m without ever bothering to go on the market. Meanwhile the rest of us are refreshing TradeMe for a $650-a-week two-bedroom and losing to nine other applications. Herne Bay operates on its own weather system, financially speaking.

Per OneRoof (21 Sep 2026): the 404sqm, five-bedroom villa on Herne Bay Road, owned via Speargrass Holdings, sold to Greymouth Holdings; QV records show the sale completed in late May. Wall Real Estate handled the deal and declined to comment further.
